findings.issue_text: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb (~lines 107-109, unsubscribe action), TopicUser.find_by result is used immediately without a nil guard, so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists for the current user (e.g., a second account opening a forwarded link, staff sampling the URL, or a cleaned-up row), producing a 500 error instead of the unsubscribe UI; should use an upsert (TopicUser.change) or nil-guard

In config/locales/server.en.yml (~line 1852, unsubscribe_link) and lib/email/message_builder.rb (~line 62), the unsubscribe_link locale now hard-requires %{unsubscribe_url} and I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument, but MessageBuilder#html_part calls it unconditionally for any mailer with add_unsubscribe_link: true while only send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url (no default added to @template_args), so any other mailer using add_unsubscribe_link: true throws at email-build time and that entire email class silently stops being delivered

In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/app-route-map.js.es6 (line 13) vs templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs (line 1), the template path doesn't match the route name: the top-level topicUnsubscribe route looks up the dasherized template topic-unsubscribe.hbs, but the template was placed at the nested path templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs (which corresponds to a topic.unsubscribe route), so the route renders with no template at all, producing a blank page with no confirmation UI; the template should be renamed or the route nested unless the resolver falls back

In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb (lines 109-115), the unsubscribe GET endpoint acts as a state-changing toggle, so reloading or re-visiting the URL mutates state again: a plain page refresh re-runs the toggle and escalates regular to muted (a heavier state the user never chose), bookmarking or re-clicking the email link causes further unintended level changes, and GET-based prefetchers/scanners can trigger it; the GET should be idempotent or the mutation should happen once

In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb (lines 109-115) vs server.en.yml (~line 1855) and client.en.yml (topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications), the copy promises users will 'stop receiving notifications' but watching/tracking users are only demoted to regular, not muted, and regular-level users still receive notifications (and emails) for direct replies, mentions, and quotes in that topic — a trust-breaking mismatch between the written guarantee and the actual state transition; either mute the topic or reword the copy

Unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET with no CSRF protection (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-114): GETs are exempt from Rails CSRF protection, so any third-party page can embed the unsubscribe URL as an image tag to silently change a logged-in user's topic notification level, and it's trivially loopable across topic IDs, causing write/render amplification on an endpoint hit at email volume

The unsubscribe action is non-idempotent: reload/revisit of the same URL keeps stepping notification levels down (watch, then regular, then muted), so a bookmarked confirmation page keeps firing save! plus the full page render

Each unsubscribe click fully materializes the topic page (TopicView.new loads topic + page of posts + details/participants, full TopicViewSerializer walked and MultiJson.dump'd, entire JSON blob embedded in the HTML response) even though templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs only consumes fancyTitle and the notification state, wasting potentially hundreds of KB (~10x what the two-sentence page needs) per response on a bursty email-CTA endpoint
The redirect path builds TopicView before issuing the 301 to the canonical URL (topics_controller.rb:99-102), wasting the full materialization on redirected requests
If PostStream.loadTopicView (routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:4) doesn't consult PreloadStore, the server pays the topic serialization a second time via the JSON XHR - needs verification

The shared unsubscribe_link locale string now hard-requires %{unsubscribe_url} (config/locales/server.en.yml + lib/email/message_builder.rb), but only send_notification_email was updated to pass it; any other mail path that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and the entire email class fails to send - every add_unsubscribe_link call site (digests, system messages) must be verified before merge

current_user.id is dereferenced unguarded in the unsubscribe action (topics_controller.rb ~103), relying entirely on the pre-existing before_filter list actually being ensure_logged_in; if it's any other filter, every logged-out click from an email (the most common way users open unsubscribe links) returns a 500

tu (the TopicUser.find_by result) is used with no nil check, so a logged-in user with no topic_users row (e.g., notified via category watch without an email-triggered TopicUser.change) raises NoMethodError, causing a full 500-render plus exception-notify churn on an email-CTA endpoint that link scanners probe

Shared email locale key 'unsubscribe_link' in config/locales/server.en.yml now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email in user_notifications.rb passes unsubscribe_url — all other mailers setting add_unsubscribe_link: true (e.g., the digest mailer) will raise I18n MissingInterpolationArgument while building the HTML part and fail to send

The new unsubscribe routes (get 't/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe' and 't/:topic_id/unsubscribe') mutate state on GET with check_xhr explicitly skipped, making them CSRF-bypassable — any third-party page can embed an img tag pointing at the endpoint and silently change a logged-in user's notification level for arbitrary topics (watching to regular, regular to muted)

The emailed promise to 'stop receiving notifications' is not fulfilled for watching/tracking users — the endpoint only downgrades them to 'regular', which still receives direct-reply/mention/quote emails, so the email footer and landing page copy mismatch the endpoint's actual behavior

The unsubscribe URL is just '/t/<id>/unsubscribe' with no per-user token (unlike the email-preferences unsubscribe key) and relies solely on session auth — a logged-out click either bounces to /login losing the deep link, or current_user.id on nil causes a 500 on the feature's primary flow

TopicUser.find_by(...) in topics_controller can return nil for a logged-in user without a TopicUser row for that topic, and the immediate tu.notification_level call raises NoMethodError, producing an unhandled 500 reachable via guessed sequential topic ids

The notification_level mutation uses tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change, which publishes MessageBus '/topic/<id>' with notification_level_change — the new path silently skips the MessageBus event, so open tabs and clients relying on it see a stale notification button until reload

Template placement at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs is inconsistent with the flat 'topicUnsubscribe' route (which resolves to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs under standard Ember naming), so the unsubscribe page may render empty without its template — the controller, view, and template file naming conventions are mutually inconsistent for any single resolution scheme

`topics_controller.rb:105-113`: the `unsubscribe` action 500s with NoMethodError when `TopicUser.find_by(user_id, topic_id)` returns nil — the very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level` with no nil-check and nothing creates the row first, so users with no existing TopicUser record (e.g. group-mention email recipients or anyone navigating directly to the URL) get a 500 instead of an unsubscribe page. Fix: nil-check and fall back to `muted`, or create the row via `TopicUser.change`.

`topics_controller.rb:98-116`: the unsubscribe mutation is non-idempotent — it *toggles* rather than sets the level, so a `tracking`/`watching` user clicking the email link lands on `regular`, and pressing F5 or re-opening the link runs it again and flips them to `muted`.

`topics_controller.rb:98-116`: the first unsubscribe click only moves `tracking`/`watching` users to `regular`, which does not stop direct reply/mention notifications, contradicting the email copy that says "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic".

`topics_controller.rb:98-116`: the state-changing mutation runs on a plain GET with no nonce/token validation, so it is CSRF-able — an `` on an external page silently flips notification levels for any logged-in user who views it, and corporate mail scanners/AV that prefetch links trigger the mutation without a click.

`config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1856` + `lib/email/message_builder.rb:~63-70`: the shared `unsubscribe_link` locale now hard-requires the `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation key — any mailer or plugin building an email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` that doesn't pass `unsubscribe_url` raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` inside the email-delivery background job, which fails and retries while the message is never delivered. Safer: default `unsubscribe_url` (e.g. fall back to the preferences URL) when absent.

`routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:4-9`: `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` has no `.catch`/error action — if the topic is deleted, is an inaccessible PM, or the server 500s, the promise rejects unhandled and the user arriving from the email sees a blank page with no feedback.

`topics_controller.rb:107-113`: the notification-level write goes through `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`, so no `notification_level_change` MessageBus event is published on `/topic/<id>` — the user's other open sessions of the topic keep showing the stale notification level until refresh.

`routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` + `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:2-4`: when the unsubscribe URL is reached via in-app client-side routing (e.g. link pasted in a post/chat and clicked in-app), the Ember route loads the topic via `topics#show`, which performs no mutation — yet the page copy asserts "You will stop receiving notifications for…", claiming an unsubscribe that never happened.

The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action ships with zero test coverage: nothing tests the toggle semantics for each starting level (watching/tracking → regular; regular/muted → muted), the slug-mismatch/blank-slug 301 redirect path vs. the toggle-and-render path, HTML vs. JSON format handling, access control (anonymous visitors, logged-in users without access to a private topic), or the rendered show response after `perform_show_response`.

Unsubscribing from a watching topic only drops the user to `regular`, where they still receive reply/mention notifications, contradicting the email's 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' promise — no spec enumerating the four starting levels forces this semantic decision to be explicit.

Anonymous visitors trigger a 500 on the unsubscribe endpoint: unsubscribe is a public GET with no login requirement, so `current_user` is nil and `current_user.id` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:106-108) raises NoMethodError; unsubscribe URLs embedded in emails mean bots and email-scanner prefetching will hit this constantly, and no test covers logged-out requests.

Logged-in users with no `TopicUser` record (e.g., manually visiting the unsubscribe URL for a topic they never interacted with) trigger a 500 because `tu.notification_level` is called on nil; no test exercises the no-TopicUser-record case.

The updated `message_builder_spec` (`let(:message_with_unsubscribe)`) passes `unsubscribe_url` but has no `html_override`, so `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` returns early at `return unless html_override = @opts[:html_override]` and the changed code interpolating `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link')` / gsubbing `%{unsubscribe_link}` is never executed — the test verifies an input, not behavior.

The `List-Unsubscribe header` `be_present` assertion in the message_builder spec doesn't verify the per-topic unsubscribe URL value at all — it would pass even if the header pointed at the preferences page or garbage.

`user_notifications` mailer specs were not updated to assert the rendered body contains `post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, nor that `Topic#unsubscribe_url` produces `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` matching the routes — a URL-construction regression would ship broken unsubscribe links in every notification email undetected.

The `unsubscribe_link` locale now hard-requires `%{unsubscribe_url}` (I18n raises `MissingInterpolationArgument` if absent), so any other email path (digest mailer, plugins, future callers) setting `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without the new opt crashes at build time instead of sending; no test exercises `html_part` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`, or proves the remaining callers still build.

The `topicUnsubscribe` route is registered after the `topic` resource, whose nested dynamic-segment routes (`fromParamsNear` at `/:nearPost` and its sibling post-number route) already match `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` — Ember matches in definition order, so the unsubscribe page may be shadowed and never render (users land on the topic route with `nearPost: 'unsubscribe'`); no routing/acceptance test asserts `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` resolves to `topicUnsubscribe`.

The new frontend route/controller/template ship with no unit tests: nothing covers the route's `model` hook (`store.createRecord` + `updateFromJson`), `afterModel` (nulling `details.notificationReasonText`), or the controller's `stopNotificiationsText` computed property — e.g., that the topic details required by `topic-notifications-button` are present or that title interpolation produces the expected text.

The `dropdown-button` conditional-title change omits the `<h4 class='title'>` element when `title` is falsy, altering the DOM for all existing consumers of this shared component (not just the new unsubscribe page), with no unit test covering either branch or confirming existing consumers are unaffected.

Unguarded `TopicUser.find_by` in the new `unsubscribe` action (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-107): it returns nil when no TopicUser row exists and the code immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level`, causing a NoMethodError/hard 500 on a link included in every notification email (reachable via shared-machine logins as a different account, or mention/reply recipients with no row).

Second crash path in the same action: `notification_level` is nullable — `TopicUser.track_visit!` creates rows without a level and the `tracking` scope's COALESCE confirms nulls are expected — so `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` becomes `nil > 1` and raises NoMethodError even when the row exists.

Verification needed: `:unsubscribe` was appended to the filter list at topics_controller.rb:24-30, but the head of that list isn't in this diff — if it isn't `ensure_logged_in`, anonymous clicks on the emailed unsubscribe link crash on `current_user.id`.

State-changing GET request (config/routes.rb:439-441 + topics_controller.rb:98): the unsubscribe toggle runs on GET, which Rails' CSRF protection never checks, enabling cross-site CSRF via ``, silent unsubscribes from email-scanner/webmail link prefetch, and non-idempotent reload that re-runs the toggle (regular → muted, suppressing even mentions) with no visible action; a POST or tokenized confirm step is the standard shape for emailed unsubscribe actions.

Domain logic duplicated in the controller (topics_controller.rb:106-113): the if/else level-toggle semantics belong in the model via the existing `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row when missing (preventing the nil crash) and publishes the MessageBus `/topic/{id}` `notification_level_change` event — the inline version loses that event (other open tabs show a stale notification level) and leaves two divergent implementations to keep in sync.

Locale now hard-requires a caller-supplied interpolation argument: `unsubscribe_link` in config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but MessageBuilder's base `template_args` (lib/email/message_builder.rb:24-28,64) provides no default, so any caller setting `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without passing `unsubscribe_url` raises `MissingInterpolationArgument` at email-build time, killing the send — an unenforced hard contract at the builder boundary.

Misspelled controller↔template contract identifier `stopNotificiationsText` ('Notificiations') in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5 and templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 — consistently misspelled on both sides so it happens to work, but grepping for 'Notification' won't find it and a one-sided fix silently renders an empty paragraph.

Route knowledge duplicated in the model: `unsubscribe_url` in app/models/topic.rb:719-721 hardcodes the '/unsubscribe' suffix, so the URL shape now lives in three places (config/routes.rb, topic.rb, app-route-map.js.es6:13) with no named route/helper tying them together — a future route change silently breaks every emailed link.

UI concern implemented by mutating model data: `afterModel` in routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:12-14 nulls the server-serialized `topic.details.notificationReasonText` attribute purely to hide a UI string, corrupting model data for any other consumer of that field on the page; the suppression belongs in the template/component layer.

Drive-by cosmetic refactors mixed into the feature (topic_user.rb:9-13 scope reindent, topic-from-params.js.es6 var→const/whitespace churn, message_builder.rb:24-38 reformat, notification.html.erb wholesale reindent burying the only behavioral change among ~30 moved lines, client.en.yml:1017 blank-line removal) — none affect behavior but they inflate the reviewable diff and permanently shift git blame.

No tests for the new server flow: the only spec touched is message_builder_spec.rb, leaving the toggle semantics, slug/redirect handling, and the nil-`TopicUser` path in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` — precisely where the P1 crash shipped — with no coverage.

TopicUser.find_by can return nil in the unsubscribe action when a different logged-in account clicks the per-topic link (shared machine, forwarded email) and has no TopicUser row, causing NoMethodError on nil and a 500 error instead of a graceful message — no nil guard and no spec covers the unsubscribe action

Unsubscribe URL has no user binding (unsubscribe_url is identical for every recipient), so the notification-level change is applied to whoever is logged in — a user logged in as account B clicking a link from account A's email silently mutes/downgrades B's own topic state while A's subscription is untouched, and the success page falsely confirms the mutation hit the right target

State-changing GET routes (t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe) mutate TopicUser.notification_level with no CSRF protection, token, confirmation, or origin check — a third-party page can embed to silently walk every logged-in visitor's topics down watching → regular → muted, inconsistent with Discourse's convention of using PUT for other notification-state mutations (star, mute, unmute, toggle_notifications)

unsubscribe_link I18n string now hard-requires %{unsubscribe_url} and html_part cooks it unconditionally when add_unsubscribe_link is set, so any email setting add_unsubscribe_link: true without passing unsubscribe_url raises MissingInterpolationArgument during build and never gets delivered — only send_notification_email was updated, leaving other in-repo callers (e.g. digest emails) or plugin emails using Email::MessageBuilder to hard-fail

Direct tu.save! in the unsubscribe action bypasses TopicUser.change, skipping the MessageBus publish that updates watcher/tracking UI in already-open topic tabs, and any future side-effects added to change (autos, callbacks, publishes) will silently not run on this path

Confirmation text overpromises: the page unconditionally declares 'You will stop receiving notifications' but tracking/watching users land on regular and still receive direct-reply and @mention emails, with no indication of the actual resulting state or that clicking again would mute entirely (one-way ratchet: watching → regular → muted)

From the diff alone, this does not guarantee “stop receiving notifications” in all cases because it explicitly leaves some users at regular instead of muted, making the promise stricter than the implemented state change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (config/routes.rb), and implements `TopicsController#unsubscribe` which toggles and `save!`s `TopicUser.notification_level` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). This is a state-changing action reachable via GET, and the controller explicitly exempts `:unsubscribe` from `:check_xhr` (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`). Since Rails CSRF protections typically don’t apply to GET requests, this endpoint can be triggered cross-site (e.g., via an `` tag) to mutate a logged-in user’s notification state without consent. The amplification concern is also grounded because it calls `perform_show_response` after saving, rendering a full topic view response.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (new action), the GET endpoint mutates state by toggling `TopicUser#notification_level` on every request: if `tu.notification_level > :regular` it sets to `:regular`, otherwise it sets to `:muted`, then `tu.save!`. This means revisiting/reloading `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` changes the user’s notification level again (e.g., watching/tracking -> regular on first visit, then regular -> muted on next), so the action is not idempotent and also performs a write on a GET route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Each unsubscribe click fully materializes the topic page (TopicView.new loads topic + page of posts + details/participants, full TopicViewSerializer walked and MultiJson.dump'd, entire JSON blob embedded in the HTML response) even though templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs only consumes fancyTitle and the notification state, wasting potentially hundreds of KB (~10x what the two-sentence page needs) per response on a bursty email-CTA endpoint

adjudication.rationale: Grounded in the diff: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` builds a full `TopicView` (`TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)`) and then calls `perform_show_response`, whose HTML path does `store_preloaded("topic_#{@topic_view.topic.id}", MultiJson.dump(topic_view_serializer))` and renders `:show`. On the client, the new `topic-unsubscribe` route/model calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and `topic.updateFromJson(json)`, which implies fetching/using the full topic-view JSON payload (including post stream) even though `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` only uses `model.fancyTitle` (via `stopNotificiationsText`) and renders `{{topic-notifications-button topic=model}}`. adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code fetches an existing `TopicUser` row (`tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)`) and then does `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`. The diff shows `TopicUser.track_visit!` can create `TopicUser` rows without `notification_level` set (`TopicUser.create(..., last_visited_at: now, first_visited_at: now)`), and the `tracking` scope uses `COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular)`, confirming `notification_level` may legitimately be NULL. If `tu.notification_level` is nil, `nil > 1` will raise (NoMethodError/ArgumentError), so this is a real crash path introduced by the new `unsubscribe` action logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: State-changing GET request (config/routes.rb:439-441 + topics_controller.rb:98): the unsubscribe toggle runs on GET, which Rails' CSRF protection never checks, enabling cross-site CSRF via ``, silent unsubscribes from email-scanner/webmail link prefetch, and non-idempotent reload that re-runs the toggle (regular → muted, suppressing even mentions) with no visible action; a POST or tokenized confirm step is the standard shape for emailed unsubscribe actions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in `config/routes.rb`) that hit `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which toggles `TopicUser.notification_level` and persists it with `tu.save!` (state-changing side effect) on a GET request. Rails’ CSRF protections generally do not apply to GET, so this is vulnerable to cross-site request triggering (e.g., ``), and also non-idempotent: reload/prefetch re-runs the toggle and can change state again. This behavior is directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Domain logic duplicated in the controller (topics_controller.rb:106-113): the if/else level-toggle semantics belong in the model via the existing `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row when missing (preventing the nil crash) and publishes the MessageBus `/topic/{id}` `notification_level_change` event — the inline version loses that event (other open tabs show a stale notification level) and leaves two divergent implementations to keep in sync.

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicsController#unsubscribe` the diff adds an inline toggle on a `TopicUser` row:
```rb
 tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])
 ...
 tu.save!
```
This can crash if `tu` is `nil` (no guard/creation shown in the diff), whereas `TopicUser.change` explicitly handles creation on missing rows (it rescues `RecordNotUnique` and is designed for updates/creates). Also, the inline `save!` bypasses the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... })` that `TopicUser.change` emits when `notification_level` changes, so other clients relying on that event can become stale. This is a behavior/regression risk directly grounded in the diff (missing publish + potential nil).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `unsubscribe_link` require `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml) while `Email::MessageBuilder`’s base `@template_args` does not provide a default `unsubscribe_url` (lib/email/message_builder.rb). However, within this diff the shown caller (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email`) and the spec were updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, so an actual failure path isn’t directly demonstrated here—this is a real API/contract sharp edge introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe URL has no user binding (unsubscribe_url is identical for every recipient), so the notification-level change is applied to whoever is logged in — a user logged in as account B clicking a link from account A's email silently mutes/downgrades B's own topic state while A's subscription is untouched, and the success page falsely confirms the mutation hit the right target

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a per-topic unsubscribe link to emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` in `user_notifications.rb`, rendered via `%{unsubscribe_link}`), but `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is just `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`, identical for all recipients. The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action applies changes to `current_user` only (`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then toggles `notification_level`). There is no per-recipient token or user binding in the URL/params, so clicking the link while logged in as a different account will mutate that logged-in account’s topic notification state, matching the finding’s described behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: State-changing GET routes (t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe) mutate TopicUser.notification_level with no CSRF protection, token, confirmation, or origin check — a third-party page can embed to silently walk every logged-in visitor's topics down watching → regular → muted, inconsistent with Discourse's convention of using PUT for other notification-state mutations (star, mute, unmute, toggle_notifications)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two **GET** routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) mapped to `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb). That controller action **mutates server state** by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` for `current_user` and calling `tu.save!` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). Because this is a GET endpoint and the diff shows no CSRF token, confirmation step, or origin/referrer validation, it is susceptible to cross-site request triggering (e.g., an embedded image/link), and it also deviates from the existing convention in the same file of using PUT for state changes (e.g., `star`).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the PR updates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is the centralized path that publishes a MessageBus event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set (`MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)`). By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, this unsubscribe path will not emit that publish, so other already-open clients/tabs subscribed to that topic channel won’t get the notification-level update in real time, and any other shared side effects in `change` won’t run for this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Confirmation text overpromises: the page unconditionally declares 'You will stop receiving notifications' but tracking/watching users land on regular and still receive direct-reply and @mention emails, with no indication of the actual resulting state or that clicking again would mute entirely (one-way ratchet: watching → regular → muted)

adjudication.rationale: The new unsubscribe page text is unconditional: client locale `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` says "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}." and the template renders it (`{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`). But the server action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` does not always mute the topic; it sets `TopicUser.notification_level` to `:regular` when the current level is above regular (e.g., watching/tracking), and only sets `:muted` otherwise. Therefore after clicking the unsubscribe link, some users will end up in `regular` rather than fully muted, contradicting the page’s promise to “stop receiving notifications” for the topic.
